Compare: taking-in is dependent and passive, taking-hold is independent and eager to learn, and letting-go is acceptance of the new roles.

A is wrong: Reviewing labor and being dependent are features of taking-in.

B is wrong: A focus on her own comfort, rest, and food shows the taking-in phase.

D is wrong: Initiating care while seeking reassurance is the taking-hold phase.

151. A woman at 30 weeks of pregnancy at a Quezon City clinic asks how to wear her seatbelt in a car. Which instruction is correct?

A. Place the lap belt below the abdomen across the hips and the shoulder strap across the trunk

B. Place the lap belt over the top of the abdomen and avoid the shoulder strap

C. Wear only the shoulder strap under the arm to avoid pressure on the baby

D. Skip the seatbelt, since the airbag protects the baby fully

Answer: A. Place the lap belt below the abdomen across the hips and the shoulder strap across the trunk

Pregnant women should always wear a seatbelt. The lap belt goes below the abdomen, snug across the hips, and the shoulder strap goes across the trunk, between the breasts and to the side of the abdomen. Never place the belt over the dome of the uterus, because a crash can cause abruptio placentae. Airbags are not a replacement for belts. Remember: lap low, shoulder strap across the chest.

B is wrong: A belt across the top of the abdomen can injure the uterus and placenta in a crash.

C is wrong: The shoulder strap should be used with the lap belt, since a lap belt alone offers less protection.

D is wrong: Airbags do not replace seatbelts, and skipping one raises maternal and fetal risk.

152. A pregnant woman tells the nurse at a Cebu hospital that she does not wear a seatbelt for short trips to the market. What is the best response?

A. A seatbelt is not needed when driving slowly in the barangay

B. A seatbelt is needed only on long trips outside the city

C. A seatbelt is needed only during the third trimester

D. A seatbelt is needed on every trip, no matter how short the distance

Answer: D. A seatbelt is needed on every trip, no matter how short the distance

Most car crashes occur close to home and at low speed, so seatbelts must be worn on every trip regardless of distance or speed. The best protection of the fetus is protecting the mother, and properly worn belts reduce maternal death and fetal loss. Also advise adjusting the seat and taking stretch breaks on long rides. Tip: short trip or long, belt on.

A is wrong: Crashes can occur even at low speed on a barangay road, so belts are always needed.

B is wrong: Short trips are common crash sites, so belts are needed at all distances.

C is wrong: Belts are needed in all trimesters, not just the third.

153. A woman at 10 weeks of gestation plans a trip by air and asks when the best time to travel during pregnancy is. The nurse replies that it is

A. During the first trimester, when she has the most energy

B. During the second trimester, when risks of miscarriage are lowest

C. Any time, since travel has no effect on the course of pregnancy

D. During the third trimester, when the baby is already mature enough

Answer: B. During the second trimester, when risks of miscarriage are lowest

The second trimester (weeks 14 to 28) is the best time to travel, because nausea is gone, energy returns, and the risks of miscarriage and preterm labor are lower. Airplane travel is generally safe until about 36 weeks if there are no complications, but airlines often require a medical certificate near term. Advise walking and stretching every 1 to 2 hours to prevent thrombosis, drinking fluids, and carrying prenatal records.

A is wrong: The first trimester has more nausea and a higher miscarriage risk.

C is wrong: Travel does matter, and timing and precautions reduce risks.

D is wrong: The third trimester raises the risk of preterm labor away from care.

154. A woman at 24 weeks with an uncomplicated pregnancy asks if she may continue swimming at a resort in Davao. What should the nurse say?

A. Swimming is allowed only if she wears a special belly support belt

B. Swimming is allowed only during the first trimester of pregnancy

C. Swimming is allowed and is a safe exercise in a normal pregnancy

D. Swimming is prohibited because water may enter the uterus

Answer: C. Swimming is allowed and is a safe exercise in a normal pregnancy

Pregnant clients are allowed to swim. The water supports body weight, relieves back strain and leg swelling, and carries a low risk of injury. Exceptions include bleeding, ruptured membranes, placenta previa, and preterm labor. Advise her to avoid diving, hot tubs, and overheating, and to rest when tired. Water does not enter the uterus through the intact cervix and mucus plug.

A is wrong: A belly support is not required for swimming.

B is wrong: Swimming is allowed throughout a normal pregnancy, not only in the first trimester.

D is wrong: Water does not enter the uterus through an intact cervix and mucus plug.

155. A couple at a barangay health center asks about sexual intercourse at 20 weeks in a normal pregnancy. Which advice by the nurse is correct?

A. Intercourse should be avoided throughout pregnancy to protect the fetus

B. Intercourse is safe if there is no bleeding, and side-to-side or rear-entry positions are comfortable

C. Intercourse is safest during the third trimester with the woman lying on her back

D. Intercourse is safe only if the couple uses oral sex that includes blowing air into the vagina

Answer: B. Intercourse is safe if there is no bleeding, and side-to-side or rear-entry positions are comfortable

In a normal pregnancy, intercourse is safe unless there is bleeding or another contraindication, and the second trimester is the best time. Side-to-side or rear-entry positions avoid abdominal pressure, and the supine position is avoided late in pregnancy. Orgasm may release prostaglandins, which can cause contractions, a concern in preterm labor. Condoms are advised to reduce infection risk.

A is wrong: Intercourse is not prohibited in a normal pregnancy, and it does not harm the fetus protected by amniotic fluid.

C is wrong: The supine position in late pregnancy compresses the vena cava, and the second trimester is better than the third.

D is wrong: Blowing air into the vagina can cause air embolism, so it is not a safe alternative.

156. Which pregnant woman should be advised to avoid sexual intercourse?

A. A woman at 20 weeks with mild morning sickness

B. A woman at 12 weeks with a history of a normal delivery

C. A woman at 34 weeks with premature rupture of the membranes

D. A woman at 26 weeks whose pregnancy has been normal

Answer: C. A woman at 34 weeks with premature rupture of the membranes

Intercourse is contraindicated with bleeding, placenta previa, premature rupture of membranes (risk of infection), preterm labor, incompetent cervix, and a history of repeated miscarriage. Semen contains prostaglandins and orgasm causes contractions, which may worsen preterm labor. In a normal pregnancy it is allowed. Remember the handout list: repeated miscarriage, incompetent cervix, bleeding, preterm labor, previa, and PROM.

A is wrong: Mild morning sickness is not a contraindication to intercourse.

B is wrong: A previous normal delivery does not restrict intercourse when this pregnancy is normal.

D is wrong: A normal pregnancy without complications allows intercourse.

157. Why should the nurse advise a couple to avoid blowing air into the vagina during sex play while the woman is pregnant?

A. Air can cause infection of the cord and the placenta

B. Air can trigger a drop in the fetal heart rate through the cervix

C. Air can cause the amniotic sac to rupture prematurely

D. Air can enter the maternal circulation and cause a fatal air embolism

Answer: D. Air can enter the maternal circulation and cause a fatal air embolism

During pregnancy the uterus and vagina are highly vascular, and forced air can enter open blood vessels at the placental site, leading to a venous air embolism that can cause sudden collapse and death of the mother and fetus. Counsel couples to avoid oral sex that involves blowing air into the vagina. Signs of embolism include sudden dyspnea, chest pain, and cyanosis.

A is wrong: Air embolism is not an infection of the cord or placenta.

B is wrong: The hazard is air entering blood vessels, not changes in fetal heart rate through the cervix.

C is wrong: Air does not rupture the intact membranes, and the risk is vascular.

158. According to the DOH 1-2-5 prenatal visit schedule, how many visits should a woman have in each trimester?

A. 3 visits in the first trimester, 3 in the second, and 2 in the third

B. 2 visits in the first trimester, 2 in the second, and 4 in the third

C. 1 visit in the first trimester, 1 in the second, and 6 in the third

D. 1 visit in the first trimester, 2 in the second, and 5 in the third

Answer: D. 1 visit in the first trimester, 2 in the second, and 5 in the third

The 1-2-5 schedule gives at least 8 prenatal visits: 1 as early as possible in the first trimester, 2 in the second, and 5 in the third, with visits becoming more frequent near term as risks rise. The visits allow early detection of complications, tetanus toxoid, micronutrient supplements, and health teaching. The digits themselves are the clue, since 1, 2, and 5 add up to 8 contacts.

A is wrong: Three first trimester visits and only two in the third does not follow the schedule, which increases frequency near term.

B is wrong: That schedule adds up to 8, but the distribution of 2, 2, and 4 does not match 1-2-5.

C is wrong: One visit in the second trimester is too few, and 6 in the third is not the 1-2-5 pattern.

159. A woman is registered at a Quezon City health center at 8 weeks of pregnancy, which is her first prenatal visit. Following the 1-2-5 schedule, how many total visits should she have completed by the end of the second trimester?

A. 2 visits

B. 5 visits

C. 8 visits

D. 3 visits

Answer: D. 3 visits

The DOH 1-2-5 schedule counts 1 visit in the first trimester and 2 in the second, so by the end of the second trimester she should have 3 visits. The remaining 5 visits fall in the third trimester, giving a total of at least 8. Encourage early registration, and make sure each visit includes BP, weight, fundal height, FHT, tetanus toxoid, and iron supplements.

A is wrong: Two visits leaves out one of the scheduled visits.

B is wrong: Five visits is the third trimester number, not the cumulative count by the second trimester.

C is wrong: Eight visits is the total for the whole pregnancy, not by the second trimester.

160. The nurse prepares tetanus toxoid for a pregnant woman at a barangay health center. Which dose and route is correct?

A. 1 mL intramuscularly

B. 0.1 mL intradermally

C. 0.5 mL intramuscularly

D. 0.5 mL subcutaneously

Answer: C. 0.5 mL intramuscularly

Tetanus toxoid (TT) is given in a dose of 0.5 mL intramuscularly, usually in the deltoid of the upper arm. Pregnant women should receive at least 2 doses, as early as possible, to protect both mother and newborn from tetanus neonatorum through passive transfer of antibodies. Shake the vial, and check the expiry date and cold chain. The vaccine is not given IV or intradermally. Exam tip: TT is 0.5 mL IM.

A is wrong: One mL is double the standard dose.

B is wrong: Intradermal injection is used for BCG, and 0.1 mL is not the TT dose.

D is wrong: The subcutaneous route is not used for TT, which is given intramuscularly.

161. A pregnant woman at 12 weeks received her first dose of tetanus toxoid (TT1) today at a health center in Cebu. When is the earliest she can receive TT2?

A. At the next prenatal visit, even if only 1 week later

B. At least 4 weeks after TT1

C. At least 6 months after TT1

D. At least 1 year after TT1

Answer: B. At least 4 weeks after TT1

TT2 is given at least 4 weeks after TT1 and ideally before delivery, protecting about 80 percent of newborns against tetanus for about 3 years. TT1 gives no protection yet. TT3 follows at least 6 months after TT2, TT4 at least 1 year after TT3, and TT5 at least 1 year after TT4. Remember the intervals: 4 weeks, 6 months, 1 year, 1 year.

A is wrong: Giving TT2 before 4 weeks is too early and does not give the expected immune response.

C is wrong: Six months is the minimum interval from TT2 to TT3, not from TT1 to TT2.

D is wrong: One year is the interval between TT3 and TT4, and between TT4 and TT5.

162. A woman received TT2 two years ago. Which statement about giving TT3 is correct?

A. It is given at least 1 year after TT2 and protects for 10 years

B. It is given at least 4 weeks after TT2 and protects for 3 years

C. It is given at least 6 months after TT2 and protects for about 5 years

D. It is given at least 6 months after TT2 and protects for life

Answer: C. It is given at least 6 months after TT2 and protects for about 5 years

TT3 is given at least 6 months after TT2, and the duration of protection is 5 years. The full list is TT1 none, TT2 3 years, TT3 5 years, TT4 10 years, and TT5 lifetime. Each dose raises the antibody level and the percent protected. Because she had TT2 two years ago, TT3 is already due and should be given as soon as possible in the pregnancy.

A is wrong: TT3 is not delayed to one year, and the 10 year protection comes with TT4.

B is wrong: Four weeks is the interval for TT2, and that protection lasts 3 years only.

D is wrong: Lifetime protection is reached only after TT5.

163. A woman in a Davao barangay has completed TT1 to TT4. Which action about TT5 is correct?

A. Give TT5 at least 6 months after TT4, which provides protection for 5 years

B. Give TT5 at least 1 year after TT4, which provides lifetime protection

C. No more doses are needed because TT4 gives lifetime protection

D. Give TT5 only during a pregnancy, which provides protection for 10 years

Answer: B. Give TT5 at least 1 year after TT4, which provides lifetime protection

TT5 is given at least 1 year after TT4 and confers lifetime protection, with about 99 percent protection. TT4 protects for about 10 years. A woman with five documented doses needs no more TT for future pregnancies. Record doses on the TT card and the maternal record. Memory aid: TT1 none, TT2 3 years, TT3 5 years, TT4 10 years, TT5 lifetime.

A is wrong: Six months is the TT2 to TT3 interval, and TT5 lasts longer than 5 years.

C is wrong: TT4 protects for about 10 years and not for life.

D is wrong: TT5 can be given whether or not she is pregnant and gives lifetime protection.

164. A newborn's mother completed TT2 during pregnancy. Approximately what protection against neonatal tetanus does this give?

A. About 99 percent for 10 years

B. About 99 percent for a lifetime

C. About 80 percent for 3 years

D. No protection until TT3 is given

Answer: C. About 80 percent for 3 years

Per the DOH schedule, TT2 protects about 80 percent for about 3 years. TT1 offers no protection yet, TT4 gives 99 percent for 10 years, and TT5 gives 99 percent for life. Maternal IgG crosses the placenta and protects the newborn from tetanus neonatorum, which is why TT2 at least 2 weeks before delivery is the minimum goal. Also teach clean cord care.

A is wrong: Ninety-nine percent for 10 years is reached with TT4.

B is wrong: Lifetime 99 percent protection is only reached with TT5.

D is wrong: TT2 already confers protection, and the benefit does not wait for TT3.

165. A woman at 10 weeks of pregnancy at a barangay health center asks about vitamin A capsules she heard are given in pregnancy. According to the handout, what should the nurse advise?

A. Vitamin A 10,000 IU is given twice a week starting on the 4th month

B. Vitamin A 10,000 IU is given daily from the first visit

C. Vitamin A is not given in pregnancy and is only for the infant

D. Vitamin A 10,000 IU is given twice a week starting immediately

Answer: A. Vitamin A 10,000 IU is given twice a week starting on the 4th month

The handout lists vitamin A 10,000 IU twice a week beginning in the 4th month, with a warning not to give it before then because high doses in early pregnancy are teratogenic and can cause birth defects. Excess vitamin A should be avoided. Current WHO guidance recommends vitamin A in pregnancy only where deficiency is a public health problem, so follow current DOH orders. Exam tip: vitamin A starts after the 3rd month.

B is wrong: Daily dosing from the first visit exceeds the schedule and risks teratogenicity in early pregnancy.

C is wrong: Vitamin A is part of the prenatal regimen after the 4th month, so saying it is not given is incorrect for this handout.

D is wrong: Starting immediately in the first trimester is unsafe, so supplementation waits until the 4th month.

166. A pregnant woman taking a daily iron tablet reports dark green-black stools and constipation. Which response by the nurse is best?

A. Explain the effects are expected, and advise fluids, fiber, and vitamin C with iron

B. Advise taking the tablet with milk or tea to reduce stomach upset

C. Tell her to stop the iron and report to the physician immediately

D. Explain that black stools mean gastrointestinal bleeding and need testing

Answer: A. Explain the effects are expected, and advise fluids, fiber, and vitamin C with iron

Iron salts commonly darken the stool and cause constipation, nausea, and heartburn, which are not harmful. The DOH gives iron (60 mg with 400 mcg folic acid) daily to prevent anemia. Increase fluids, fiber, and activity, and take iron on an empty stomach or with vitamin C such as calamansi juice to boost absorption. Avoid taking it with milk, coffee, or tea, which reduce absorption, and keep it away from children, since overdose is toxic.

B is wrong: Milk, tea, and coffee bind iron and reduce absorption.

C is wrong: Stopping iron is unnecessary and risks anemia, since these effects are expected.

D is wrong: Dark stools from iron are harmless, and bleeding would also show other signs.

167. A woman at a clinic in Cebu is planning to conceive. Which supplement and daily dose should the nurse recommend to prevent neural tube defects?

A. Vitamin D 600 to 2000 IU daily

B. Iodine 150 mcg daily

C. Folic acid 400 to 800 mcg daily

D. Calcium 1000 to 1300 mg daily

Answer: C. Folic acid 400 to 800 mcg daily

Folic acid, 400 to 800 mcg daily, prevents neural tube defects such as spina bifida and anencephaly. The neural tube closes by about 28 days after conception, often before the woman knows she is pregnant, so supplementation should begin at least 1 month before conception and continue through the first trimester. Good food sources are green leafy vegetables and legumes. Women with a prior affected child need a higher prescribed dose.

A is wrong: Vitamin D supports calcium absorption and bone health, not closure of the neural tube.

B is wrong: Iodine supports thyroid function and fetal brain development.

D is wrong: Calcium builds fetal bones and teeth and maintains maternal bone health.

168. A nurse explains why a pregnant woman needs 1000 to 1300 mg of calcium daily. What is its main purpose?

A. Prevention of neural tube defects in the first trimester

B. Prevention of iron deficiency anemia in the mother

C. Fetal bone and teeth development and the mother's bone health

D. Support of fetal thyroid function and brain development

Answer: C. Fetal bone and teeth development and the mother's bone health

The fetus draws calcium from the mother to build bones and teeth, especially in the third trimester, so extra calcium protects the mother's bone density too. Recommended intake is 1000 to 1300 mg daily from milk, small fish eaten with bones (dilis), malunggay, and tofu. Vitamin D improves absorption. Spacing calcium at least 2 hours from iron helps both to be absorbed. Remember: calcium is for bones and teeth.

A is wrong: Neural tube defect prevention is the role of folic acid.

B is wrong: Anemia is prevented with iron, and calcium actually competes with iron absorption.

D is wrong: Thyroid and brain development relate to iodine.

169. A woman in a coastal town asks the nurse why iodine is part of her prenatal supplements. Which explanation is correct?

A. It helps the body absorb calcium, at 150 mcg daily

B. It builds fetal bones and teeth, at 150 mcg daily

C. It supports closure of the neural tube, at 150 mcg daily

D. It supports thyroid function and fetal brain development, at 150 mcg daily

Answer: D. It supports thyroid function and fetal brain development, at 150 mcg daily

Iodine, 150 mcg per day in pregnancy, is needed to make thyroid hormones that drive fetal brain and nervous system development. Deficiency can lead to cretinism, stillbirth, and impaired intelligence, which is why iodized salt (asin) is promoted in the Philippines. Folic acid prevents neural tube defects, calcium builds bones, and vitamin D aids calcium absorption. Exam tip: iodine goes with thyroid and brain.

A is wrong: Calcium absorption depends on vitamin D.

B is wrong: Bone and teeth building is the role of calcium.

C is wrong: Neural tube closure depends on folic acid.

170. A woman at 6 weeks of pregnancy tells the nurse at a Davao clinic that she is still taking isotretinoin for acne. What is the priority action?

A. Reassure her since oral acne drugs are safe in pregnancy

B. Notify the physician at once, since isotretinoin is a known teratogen

C. Advise her to double the dose to finish the acne treatment

D. Tell her to take it only on alternate days to lower the risk

Answer: B. Notify the physician at once, since isotretinoin is a known teratogen

Isotretinoin (Accutane) and other retinoids are strongly teratogenic, causing craniofacial, cardiac, and central nervous system defects, especially in the first trimester. Other teratogens to memorize: thalidomide, warfarin, methotrexate, valproate, lithium, tetracyclines, ACE inhibitors and ARBs, and anticancer drugs. Stopping the drug is done under physician direction, with counseling and ultrasound evaluation. Women on such drugs need reliable contraception.

A is wrong: Isotretinoin is not safe in pregnancy and carries a high risk of birth defects.

C is wrong: Doubling the dose greatly increases fetal harm.

D is wrong: Alternate-day use does not make a teratogen safe.

171. A prenatal screening shows a rubella titer of 1:32 in a woman at a Quezon City clinic. How should the nurse interpret the result?

A. The test is invalid and must be repeated in 6 months

B. She is immune to rubella, since the titer is greater than 1:8

C. She is susceptible and needs MMR vaccine during this pregnancy

D. She has an active rubella infection and must be isolated

Answer: B. She is immune to rubella, since the titer is greater than 1:8

A rubella titer above 1:8 (many laboratories say 1:8 or higher) shows immunity from past infection or vaccination, so no action is needed. A low titer, less than 1:8, means susceptibility, and since MMR is a live attenuated vaccine, it is contraindicated in pregnancy and is given postpartum, with pregnancy avoided for 1 month. Rubella in early pregnancy causes congenital rubella syndrome: cataracts, deafness, and heart defects.

A is wrong: No repeat test is needed because the titer already shows immunity.

C is wrong: MMR is a live vaccine that is not given during pregnancy, and she is already immune.

D is wrong: A high titer does not show active infection, which needs IgM testing and symptoms.

172. A nurse in a barangay health center explains the law that guarantees universal access to maternal health care, contraception, and family planning information. Which law is this?

A. RA 10354, Responsible Parenthood and Reproductive Health Act of 2012

B. RA 10028, Expanded Breastfeeding Promotion Act of 2009

C. RA 9288, Newborn Screening Act of 2004

D. RA 7600, Rooming-in and Breastfeeding Act

Answer: A. RA 10354, Responsible Parenthood and Reproductive Health Act of 2012

RA 10354, the RPRH Law, guarantees universal access to methods of contraception, family planning information, and maternal health care. It provides for family planning services and reproductive health and sex education in the school curriculum. RA 10028 deals with breastfeeding, RA 9288 with newborn screening, and RA 7600 with rooming-in. Memory aid: RPRH goes with 10354.

B is wrong: RA 10028 promotes breastfeeding in workplaces and health institutions.

C is wrong: RA 9288 mandates newborn screening for metabolic and congenital disorders.

D is wrong: RA 7600 requires rooming-in and breastfeeding in health facilities.

173. Which provision is included in the Responsible Parenthood and Reproductive Health Act (RA 10354)?

A. Mandatory newborn screening within the first 24 to 48 hours of life

B. Lactation stations and breastfeeding breaks for working mothers

C. Reproductive health and sex education integrated in the school curriculum

D. Regulation of the advertising and marketing of breastmilk substitutes

Answer: C. Reproductive health and sex education integrated in the school curriculum

RA 10354 ensures universal access to maternal health care, contraception, and family planning, and integrates age- and development-appropriate reproductive health and sex education into the school curriculum. Newborn screening belongs to RA 9288, breastfeeding at work to RA 10028, and the Milk Code (EO 51) controls the marketing of breastmilk substitutes. Match each law with its focus for PNLE items.

A is wrong: Newborn screening is under RA 9288.

B is wrong: Workplace lactation breaks are under RA 10028.

D is wrong: Marketing of milk substitutes is covered by the Milk Code, EO 51.

174. A couple with two children at a barangay health center asks the nurse for the recommended birth spacing under the family planning program. What is the best answer based on the handout?

A. One child every 18 months

B. One child every year

C. One child every 10 years

D. One child every 3 years

Answer: D. One child every 3 years

The handout recommends spacing births at 1 child every 3 years so the mother can recover nutritionally and physically, breastfeed, and the family can manage its resources. Short intervals, less than 18 months, raise the risks of preterm birth, low birth weight, and maternal anemia. Healthy timing and spacing is part of RPRH counseling. WHO advises at least 24 months and preferably 3 to 5 years.

A is wrong: An interval of 18 months is still shorter than the 3 year recommendation.

B is wrong: Every year gives too little recovery time and raises maternal and infant risks.

C is wrong: Ten years is much longer than the recommended spacing and is not a program standard.

175. A woman returning to work in a Makati company asks the nurse about her rights as a breastfeeding employee. Which provision of RA 10028 applies?

A. Prohibition of all breastmilk substitutes in the country

B. Mandatory 3 years of paid maternity leave

C. Free infant formula provided by the employer for 6 months

D. Breastfeeding breaks and a lactation station at the workplace

Answer: D. Breastfeeding breaks and a lactation station at the workplace

RA 10028, the Expanded Breastfeeding Promotion Act of 2009, requires workplaces to provide lactation stations and time for breastfeeding or milk expression, and promotes breastfeeding in health institutions. The Milk Code (EO 51) regulates, not bans, the marketing of breastmilk substitutes. Maternity leave is covered by another law, the Expanded Maternity Leave Law, which gives 105 days. Teach mothers how to store expressed milk safely.

A is wrong: EO 51 regulates promotion and marketing of substitutes and does not ban them outright.

B is wrong: Maternity leave is separate and is 105 days, not 3 years.

C is wrong: The law supports breastfeeding and does not provide employer-funded formula.

176. A formula company representative offers free milk samples to postpartum mothers in a Cebu hospital ward. How should the nurse respond?

A. Accept the samples, since free milk helps low-income mothers

B. Decline, since the Milk Code (EO 51) regulates promotion of milk substitutes

C. Accept the samples, but give them only to mothers who cannot breastfeed

D. Decline, since RA 9288 prohibits all milk products in the hospital

Answer: B. Decline, since the Milk Code (EO 51) regulates promotion of milk substitutes

Executive Order 51, the Milk Code, regulates the marketing and distribution of breastmilk substitutes, bottles, and teats to protect breastfeeding. It prohibits free samples and promotion in health facilities and direct advertising to mothers. RA 10028 and RA 7600 also support breastfeeding in hospitals. Health workers should not distribute samples and must give sound advice on infant feeding. Violations are reported to the DOH.

A is wrong: Free samples are prohibited in health facilities and undermine breastfeeding.

C is wrong: Distribution to selected mothers still violates the Milk Code, since health workers cannot endorse or distribute samples.

D is wrong: RA 9288 is the newborn screening law and does not regulate milk products.

177. A baby is born at a lying-in clinic in Quezon City. The nurse prepares the newborn screening under RA 9288. Which procedure is correct?

A. Collect a dried blood spot from the heel at 24 to 48 hours after birth

B. Collect a venous blood sample from the arm at the age of 7 days

C. Collect a urine specimen from the newborn at 12 hours of life

D. Collect cord blood during birth and send it to the laboratory

Answer: A. Collect a dried blood spot from the heel at 24 to 48 hours after birth

RA 9288, the Newborn Screening Act of 2004, requires screening of every newborn for metabolic, congenital, and hereditary disorders. A few drops of blood from the heel are placed on special filter paper (dried blood spot) at 24 to 48 hours after birth, when the baby has had enough feeds. Screening before 24 hours may give false results, and a baby discharged early should still be screened. Memory aid: heel, 24 to 48 hours, dried blood spot.

B is wrong: A venous sample at 7 days is late and not the standard method.

C is wrong: NBS is based on blood spots and not on urine.

D is wrong: Cord blood is not the standard NBS specimen, since heel blood is used.

178. A mother in a barangay says her baby looks healthy and refuses newborn screening. What is the nurse's best explanation?

A. The test is only needed if the baby has jaundice or is premature

B. Many disorders show no signs at birth, and early detection prevents disability

C. The test is optional, since it only checks the baby's blood type

D. The test can wait until 1 year of age and give the same results

Answer: B. Many disorders show no signs at birth, and early detection prevents disability

RA 9288 makes screening mandatory because disorders such as congenital hypothyroidism, PKU, and G6PD deficiency often cause no visible signs in the first weeks, yet delayed treatment leads to intellectual disability or death. Early detection allows simple treatment, such as thyroid hormone or a special diet. Counsel respectfully, reassure her that the procedure is quick and uses only a few drops of blood, and document an informed refusal if she still declines.

A is wrong: Screening is for all newborns, not only those with jaundice or prematurity.

C is wrong: The test detects metabolic and hereditary disorders and is not just blood typing.

D is wrong: Delay to 1 year loses the window for early treatment, and screening is meant within days of birth.

179. A woman at her first prenatal visit at a health center in Davao is hesitant to have an HIV test. What is the best explanation by the nurse?

A. Testing is done only on women with a history of multiple partners

B. Testing, with counseling and consent under RA 11166, allows early treatment for mother and baby

C. Testing is delayed until the third trimester so that it does not worry the mother

D. Testing is a way to report her result to her employer and barangay

Answer: B. Testing, with counseling and consent under RA 11166, allows early treatment for mother and baby

Prenatal HIV testing is part of routine prenatal care under RA 11166, the Philippine HIV and AIDS Policy Act, because early antiretroviral therapy greatly reduces mother-to-child transmission. Pre- and post-test counseling and informed consent are required, and confidentiality must be protected. Syphilis (VDRL or RPR) and hepatitis B (HBsAg) tests are also done. Remember: test early, treat early, keep it private.

A is wrong: Universal prenatal screening applies to all pregnant women, not only those labeled high risk.

C is wrong: Delaying the test loses the chance to begin treatment early to prevent transmission.

D is wrong: Results are confidential and are not shared with employers or the barangay without consent.

180. Which prenatal laboratory test is done to screen a pregnant woman for syphilis?

A. VDRL or RPR

B. Maternal serum alpha-fetoprotein

C. Fasting blood sugar

D. HBsAg

Answer: A. VDRL or RPR

VDRL (Venereal Disease Research Laboratory) and RPR (rapid plasma reagin) are nontreponemal screening tests for syphilis, done at the first prenatal visit and repeated in the third trimester if risk exists. A reactive result is confirmed with a treponemal test and treated with penicillin to prevent congenital syphilis. HBsAg detects hepatitis B, FBS checks for diabetes, and MSAFP screens for neural tube defects.

B is wrong: MSAFP screens for neural tube defects and chromosomal disorders, not infections.

C is wrong: Fasting blood sugar checks for gestational diabetes risk.

D is wrong: HBsAg detects hepatitis B infection.

181. A woman in a Cebu hospital tests positive for HBsAg at delivery. Which action for her newborn is a priority?

A. Give hepatitis B vaccine and immune globulin as soon as possible after birth

B. Isolate the newborn and discourage skin-to-skin contact for 1 week

C. Delay hepatitis B vaccine until the baby is 6 months old

D. Give only antibiotics for the first 7 days

Answer: A. Give hepatitis B vaccine and immune globulin as soon as possible after birth

HBsAg positivity means the mother has hepatitis B infection and can transmit it at birth. The newborn should receive hepatitis B immune globulin and the first dose of hepatitis B vaccine within 12 to 24 hours of birth, which prevents infection in most infants. Standard precautions apply, and no isolation is needed. Breastfeeding is allowed once prophylaxis is given. Complete the vaccine series on schedule.

B is wrong: Isolation is not needed since standard precautions are enough and bonding is encouraged.

C is wrong: Delaying the vaccine leaves the newborn unprotected during the highest-risk period.

D is wrong: Antibiotics do not treat or prevent a viral infection such as hepatitis B.

182. A woman at 26 weeks in a Quezon City hospital has a family history of diabetes and is scheduled for a glucose tolerance test. What is the purpose of this test?

A. To measure fetal lung maturity

B. To screen for neural tube defects in the fetus

C. To detect Rh incompatibility between mother and fetus

D. To identify gestational diabetes mellitus

Answer: D. To identify gestational diabetes mellitus

The glucose tolerance test identifies gestational diabetes, which increases the risk of macrosomia, birth injury, neonatal hypoglycemia, and preeclampsia. It is commonly done at 24 to 28 weeks, earlier in high-risk women, with a glucose load and blood drawn at fasting, 1 hour, and 2 hours. Fasting blood sugar is an initial screen. Teach her to fast as instructed and to avoid smoking or strenuous exercise before the test.

A is wrong: Fetal lung maturity is assessed with amniotic fluid analysis.

B is wrong: Neural tube defects are screened using maternal serum alpha-fetoprotein and ultrasound.

C is wrong: Rh incompatibility is detected by blood typing and indirect Coombs testing.

183. A nurse at a Davao health center uses a handheld device to detect the fetal heartbeat of a woman at 11 weeks of gestation. Which device is used?

A. 4-D ultrasound

B. Standard stethoscope

C. Fetoscope

D. Doppler ultrasound

Answer: D. Doppler ultrasound

A Doppler device uses ultrasound waves to detect fetal heart motion and can pick up the heartbeat as early as 10 to 12 weeks. A fetoscope is useful only at about 18 to 20 weeks, and a regular stethoscope is not sensitive enough until later. Apply gel on the lower abdomen, and the normal fetal heart rate is 110 to 160 bpm. Transvaginal ultrasound is used in early pregnancy to confirm the pregnancy.

A is wrong: A 4-D ultrasound shows the face and movements near term and is not a handheld heart rate detector.

B is wrong: A stethoscope cannot hear the fetal heartbeat at 11 weeks.

C is wrong: A fetoscope detects heart sounds only at about 18 to 20 weeks.

184. A nurse performs a nonstress test on a woman at 34 weeks in a Cebu hospital. Which result is reactive?

A. No change in heart rate with fetal movements over 20 minutes

B. Two accelerations of at least 15 bpm lasting 15 seconds within 20 minutes with fetal movement

C. Two late decelerations of at least 15 bpm lasting 15 seconds within 20 minutes

D. One acceleration of 10 bpm lasting 10 seconds within 40 minutes

Answer: B. Two accelerations of at least 15 bpm lasting 15 seconds within 20 minutes with fetal movement

A nonstress test (NST) is noninvasive and done after 28 weeks. It is reactive (reassuring) when there are at least two accelerations of 15 bpm lasting 15 seconds in 20 minutes in response to fetal movement, which means an intact, well-oxygenated fetus. No accelerations in 40 minutes is nonreactive and needs follow-up such as a BPP or CST. Remember: 15 by 15, twice in 20.

A is wrong: No change with movement is a nonreactive result needing further testing.

C is wrong: Late decelerations are a sign of poor placental perfusion and not a reactive result.

D is wrong: One small acceleration over a longer period does not meet criteria.

185. Which statement correctly differentiates the contraction stress test (CST) from the nonstress test (NST)?

A. CST combines ultrasound with NST, and a score of 8 to 10 is good

B. CST relates the fetal heart rate to fetal movement, and a reactive result is good

C. CST is performed without contractions, and accelerations make it negative

D. CST relates the heart rate to contractions, and a negative result with no late decelerations is good

Answer: D. CST relates the heart rate to contractions, and a negative result with no late decelerations is good

The NST correlates fetal heart rate with fetal movement, and a reactive result (accelerations) is good. The CST correlates the fetal heart rate with induced uterine contractions, by oxytocin infusion or nipple stimulation, and checks whether the fetus can withstand labor. A negative CST (no late decelerations) is good, and a positive CST (repeated late decelerations) signals poor reserve. The combination of ultrasound with NST is the biophysical profile.

A is wrong: Combining ultrasound with NST describes the biophysical profile.

B is wrong: That describes the NST, not the CST.

C is wrong: CST needs contractions induced by oxytocin or nipple stimulation, and a negative result means no late decelerations.

186. Which list contains the components of the biophysical profile as remembered by the mnemonic BATMAN?

A. Bleeding, amniotic fluid, tone, maternal pulse, nonstress test

B. Breathing, amniotic fluid, tone, movement, accelerations by NST

C. Breathing, albumin, temperature, movement, accelerations

D. Blood pressure, amniotic fluid, tone, movement, antibody screen

Answer: B. Breathing, amniotic fluid, tone, movement, accelerations by NST

The biophysical profile combines ultrasound with the NST to judge fetal well-being, usually in the third trimester from about 32 weeks. The parameters are fetal Breathing movements, Amniotic fluid volume, fetal Tone, fetal body Movement, and heart rate Accelerations on the Nonstress test. Each is scored 0 or 2, for a maximum of 10. A score of 8 to 10 is reassuring, and 4 or less suggests fetal compromise.

A is wrong: Maternal bleeding and pulse are not BPP components.

C is wrong: Albumin and temperature are not parameters of the BPP.

D is wrong: Blood pressure and antibody screen are not BPP components.

187. A woman at 16 weeks in a Davao clinic has a maternal serum alpha-fetoprotein level that is higher than expected. For which condition is the fetus at higher risk?

A. Rh incompatibility

B. Neural tube defect

C. Down syndrome

D. Cystic fibrosis

Answer: B. Neural tube defect

High maternal AFP suggests a neural tube defect such as spina bifida or anencephaly (also consider wrong gestational age or twins), while low AFP is associated with Down syndrome (trisomy 21). MSAFP is a screening, not a diagnostic test, done at about 15 to 20 weeks, so abnormal results need confirmation with ultrasound and amniocentesis. Memory aid: high AFP goes with an open back, and low AFP goes with Down.

A is wrong: Rh incompatibility is detected by blood typing and antibody titer, not AFP.

C is wrong: Down syndrome is associated with low AFP, not high AFP.

D is wrong: Cystic fibrosis is evaluated by genetic and sweat testing and not by MSAFP.

188. A physician plans to check fetal chromosomes in a woman at 16 weeks. Which test is done at 14 to 20 weeks by sampling amniotic fluid?

A. Percutaneous umbilical blood sampling

B. Amniocentesis

C. Nonstress test

D. Chorionic villus sampling

Answer: B. Amniocentesis

Amniocentesis is done at 14 to 20 weeks to detect chromosomal abnormalities and neural tube defects, and later in pregnancy to assess fetal lung maturity. CVS samples the chorionic villi at 10 to 13 weeks (as early as 11), and PUBS samples fetal blood from the umbilical cord after 17 weeks, useful for Rh incompatibility. Remember CAP: Chorion, Amniotic fluid, Percutaneous cord blood.

A is wrong: PUBS samples umbilical cord blood after 17 weeks.

C is wrong: NST is a noninvasive heart rate test and does not sample fluid.

D is wrong: CVS samples placental villi at 10 to 13 weeks.

189. A woman at 17 weeks in a Quezon City hospital has just had an amniocentesis. Which finding needs the most urgent report to the physician?

A. Minor irritation at the needle puncture site

B. Mild cramping for a few hours after the procedure

C. Persistent leaking of fluid with fever and severe abdominal pain

D. Brief, minor leakage of clear fluid in the first hours

Answer: C. Persistent leaking of fluid with fever and severe abdominal pain

Mild cramping, minor irritation at the puncture site, and brief minor fluid leakage are listed side effects of amniocentesis and usually settle within 24 hours with rest. Persistent leakage, fever, severe pain, heavy bleeding, or reduced fetal movement suggest infection, rupture of membranes, or placental injury and must be reported at once. If the woman is Rh negative, Rh immune globulin is given after the procedure.

A is wrong: Minor puncture-site irritation is an expected effect.

B is wrong: Mild cramping is an expected effect and usually settles.

D is wrong: A brief minor leak is a listed side effect and is usually self-limited.

190. The nurse reviews diagnostic tests for fetal abnormalities. Which pairing of the test and its specimen source is correct?

A. Amniocentesis, chorionic villi of the placenta

B. Chorionic villus sampling, fetal blood from the umbilical vein

C. Chorionic villus sampling, chorionic villi of the placenta

D. Percutaneous umbilical blood sampling, amniotic fluid

Answer: C. Chorionic villus sampling, chorionic villi of the placenta

Use CAP. Chorionic villus sampling takes placental villi (10 to 13 weeks, as early as 11) for early chromosomal diagnosis. Amniocentesis takes amniotic fluid (14 to 20 weeks) for chromosomes, neural tube defects, and lung maturity. Percutaneous umbilical blood sampling takes umbilical vein (fetal) blood after 17 weeks for Rh disease and chromosomal studies. CVS cannot detect neural tube defects, which need AFP or amniotic fluid testing.

A is wrong: Amniocentesis samples amniotic fluid, not villi.

B is wrong: Fetal blood from the umbilical vein is obtained by PUBS, not CVS.

D is wrong: PUBS samples fetal blood from the umbilical cord, not amniotic fluid.

191. A postpartum woman in a Davao hospital, 2 days after delivery, is not breastfeeding and wants a method she can use right away for the first intercourse. What does the nurse suggest from the handout?

A. Cervical cap fitted during the stay

B. Diaphragm fitted before discharge

C. Combined oral contraceptive pills

D. Condom

Answer: D. Condom

The condom can be used immediately after delivery because it needs no fitting, no hormones, and no prescription, and it also protects against STIs. Estrogen-containing pills are delayed because of clotting risk, and a diaphragm or cervical cap must be refitted after the uterus and vagina return to normal size, at about 6 weeks. Remember: condom right away, diaphragm after 6 weeks.

A is wrong: A cervical cap also requires fitting after the cervix has returned to normal size.

B is wrong: A diaphragm needs a refit after involution, so it cannot be used immediately.

C is wrong: Combined pills contain estrogen, which raises clot risk and is delayed postpartum.

192. A woman with diabetes mellitus at a clinic in Quezon City asks about a contraceptive that does not affect blood glucose. Which choice matches the handout key points?

A. Combined oral contraceptive pills

B. Implant of progestin under the skin of the arm

C. Depot injection of progestin every 3 months

D. Barrier methods such as the diaphragm or condom

Answer: D. Barrier methods such as the diaphragm or condom

The handout lists barrier methods, the diaphragm and condom, as best for diabetic clients because they have no effect on blood glucose, lipids, or vascular disease. Hormonal methods may alter glucose metabolism, and estrogen pills raise vascular risk, though current guidelines also allow IUDs and implants for well-controlled diabetes. Whichever method she chooses, counsel on glycemic control before pregnancy to lower the risk of congenital anomalies.

A is wrong: Combined pills can alter glucose tolerance and raise vascular risk.

B is wrong: Progestin implants may affect glucose metabolism and are not the handout's best choice.

C is wrong: Progestin injections can raise blood glucose and cause weight gain.

193. A man at a barangay health center had a vasectomy last week and says he may stop using condoms. What should the nurse teach?

A. Condoms are needed only until his wound has healed in 3 days

B. The man is considered sterile immediately after the procedure

C. Use another method until 20 to 25 ejaculations have passed and sperm count is zero

D. Another method is needed for 1 year until the sperm disappear

Answer: C. Use another method until 20 to 25 ejaculations have passed and sperm count is zero

After vasectomy, sperm remain in the vas deferens beyond the cut, so a zero sperm count is attained only after 20 to 25 ejaculations (about 3 months). A semen analysis confirms sterility, and until then another method such as condoms is required. Vasectomy does not affect erection, libido, ejaculation, or testosterone, and it does not protect against STIs. Tip: 20 to 25 ejaculations to reach zero.

A is wrong: Wound healing does not determine sterility, and pregnancy can happen until sperm are cleared.

B is wrong: Sperm are still stored beyond the cut, so he is not sterile immediately.

D is wrong: One year is far longer than necessary, as sperm clear after 20 to 25 ejaculations.

194. A woman with blood pressure of 160/100 mmHg at a Cebu health center asks for oral contraceptive pills. What should the nurse do?

A. Explain that hypertension is a contraindication and advise another method

B. Start the pills together with a diuretic to keep blood pressure normal

C. Advise taking the pills at bedtime to prevent a rise in blood pressure

D. Start the pills and recheck the blood pressure after 1 year

Answer: A. Explain that hypertension is a contraindication and advise another method

Combined oral contraceptives contain estrogen, which raises blood pressure and clotting risk, so hypertension is a contraindication, along with thromboembolism, stroke, estrogen-dependent cancer, liver disease, and smoking over age 35. A woman with BP 160/100 should have the hypertension managed and be offered a safer method such as condoms or an IUD. Teach all pill users the ACHES warning signs: abdominal pain, chest pain, headache, eye problems, and severe leg pain.

B is wrong: Adding a drug to mask the effect is unsafe, and the pills are still contraindicated.

C is wrong: Taking the pills at bedtime does not reduce the effect of estrogen on blood pressure.

D is wrong: Pills can worsen hypertension and should not be started in this situation.

195. A woman started oral contraceptive pills 2 weeks ago and reports irritability and mild nausea. What is the best response?

A. Stop the pills at once and use no method for the rest of the month

B. Double the dose of the pills so that the symptoms stop sooner

C. These effects mean she has a blood clot and needs emergency care now

D. These effects are common and usually improve in 2 to 3 months, so continue the pills

Answer: D. These effects are common and usually improve in 2 to 3 months, so continue the pills

Common early effects of oral contraceptives include nausea, breast tenderness, spotting, headache, and mood changes such as irritability, due to hormone adjustment, and they usually lessen within 2 to 3 months. Taking the pill with food or at bedtime helps nausea. Danger signs to report are ACHES: abdominal pain, chest pain, severe headache, eye problems, and severe leg pain. Missing pills reduces effectiveness, so take one at the same time daily.

A is wrong: Stopping without a backup method exposes her to pregnancy, and mild effects are expected.

B is wrong: Doubling the dose increases side effects and does not improve tolerance.

C is wrong: Irritability and mild nausea are not signs of clotting, which presents as leg pain or chest pain.

196. Two days after IUD insertion at a barangay health center, a woman reports mild lower abdominal cramping and light spotting. What does the nurse tell her?

A. Cramping means she is pregnant, and the IUD must be removed at once

B. The IUD has perforated the uterus, and she needs surgery now

C. She should pull the string daily to confirm the device is firmly in place

D. These are common after insertion, but report fever, severe pain, or a missing string

Answer: D. These are common after insertion, but report fever, severe pain, or a missing string

Cramping and spotting are common side effects of IUD insertion and usually decrease in the first weeks. Teach her to check the string gently once a month after menses, and to report fever, severe pain, heavy bleeding, foul discharge, a missed period, or a missing or longer string. Fever or severe pain suggests infection or perforation. An analgesic such as ibuprofen can ease the cramps.

A is wrong: Mild cramping is not a sign of pregnancy, and the IUD is removed only if indicated.

B is wrong: Perforation causes severe pain and shock, not just mild cramping and light spotting.

C is wrong: Pulling the string daily can dislodge the device, since only a gentle monthly check is advised.

197. A woman with frequent urinary tract infections asks a nurse in a Davao clinic to fit her with a diaphragm. What should the nurse explain?

A. A diaphragm is not suitable since pressure on the urethra increases the risk of UTI

B. A diaphragm is the best choice because it protects against urinary infections

C. A diaphragm is suitable only if it is left in place for 3 days

D. A diaphragm is suitable if she takes antibiotics before every use

Answer: A. A diaphragm is not suitable since pressure on the urethra increases the risk of UTI

A diaphragm's rim can press on the urethra and trap bacteria, and spermicide can irritate tissue, so frequent UTI is a contraindication. Other contraindications include allergy to latex or spermicide, poor vaginal tone, uterine prolapse, and a history of toxic shock syndrome. It must be fitted by a trained provider, used with spermicide, left in for 6 hours after intercourse but not beyond 24 hours, and refitted after delivery or a major weight change.

B is wrong: A diaphragm does not protect against UTI and can increase the risk.

C is wrong: Leaving it in beyond 24 hours raises the risk of infection and toxic shock syndrome.

D is wrong: Routine antibiotics before use are not recommended and do not make the method suitable.

198. A woman in a Cebu clinic asks which method both prevents pregnancy and protects against HIV and other sexually transmitted infections. Which should the nurse name?

A. Oral contraceptive pills

B. Condom

C. Intrauterine device

D. Lactational amenorrhea method

Answer: B. Condom

Among these methods, the condom is the only one that prevents both pregnancy and STIs, including HIV/AIDS, because it forms a barrier to semen and vaginal fluids when used correctly with every act. Hormonal methods, IUDs, and LAM do not protect against infection. Dual protection, a condom plus another method, is advised for those at risk of STI. Teach to check the expiry date, use water-based lubricants only, and use a new condom each time.

A is wrong: Pills prevent ovulation only and do not protect against STIs.

C is wrong: An IUD prevents pregnancy but gives no protection from infections.

D is wrong: LAM relies on breastfeeding and has no protection against infection.

199. A man at a barangay health center reports severe redness, itching, and swelling of the genitals after using condoms. What should the nurse recommend?

A. Stop all contraception since his condition is permanent and untreatable

B. Use two latex condoms at once to reduce direct skin contact

C. Suspect latex allergy and switch to polyurethane condoms or another method

D. Continue the same condoms and apply a steroid cream before use

Answer: C. Suspect latex allergy and switch to polyurethane condoms or another method

Redness, itching, and swelling after condom use point to latex allergy, the only contraindication to condoms in the handout. Switch to polyurethane or polyisoprene condoms, and note that natural membrane (lambskin) condoms do not protect against HIV. Severe allergy can cause anaphylaxis, so ask about reactions to gloves or balloons. Document the allergy and alert staff to avoid latex gloves. Using two condoms increases friction and breakage.

A is wrong: Stopping contraception is unnecessary since there are many other effective methods.

B is wrong: Using two condoms increases friction and breakage and still exposes him to latex.

D is wrong: Continuing exposure can worsen to anaphylaxis, and creams do not treat the cause.

200. A woman at a Quezon City health center had a progestin implant inserted in her upper arm and, months later, reports weight gain, headache, acne, and irregular menstrual bleeding. How should the nurse interpret these?

A. Signs of pregnancy, so a pregnancy test is the only action needed

B. Expected progestin side effects, remembered as WHAM, managed with counseling

C. Signs of an implant infection that requires immediate removal of the capsules

D. Signs of an allergic reaction to the implant that need epinephrine

Answer: B. Expected progestin side effects, remembered as WHAM, managed with counseling

Norplant (progestin-only implant capsules placed under the skin of the upper arm) is effective within 24 hours after insertion and lasts about 5 years per the handout. Common side effects are summarized by WHAM: Weight gain, Headache or Hirsutism, Acne, and Menstrual bleeding changes. Counsel and reassure, and report fever, pus, or severe pain at the site. Norplant has been replaced in practice by newer implants, such as Implanon with 3 years of use.

A is wrong: These effects are expected with progestin implants and are not by themselves a sign of pregnancy.

C is wrong: Infection would show redness, pus, and fever at the insertion site, not these systemic effects.

D is wrong: These effects are hormonal and not an allergic reaction, which would show hives or breathing difficulty.

201. A woman undergoing an infertility workup at a Manila clinic learns that both of her fallopian tubes are blocked. The nurse explains that the normal function of the fallopian tubes is to

A. serve as the usual site where the embryo implants

B. produce estrogen and progesterone during each cycle

C. transport the ovum from the ovary toward the uterus

D. secrete the mucus that changes at ovulation

Answer: C. transport the ovum from the ovary toward the uterus

The fallopian tubes carry the egg released by the ovary toward the uterus, and fertilization normally takes place in the outer part of the tube. When both tubes are blocked, sperm and ovum cannot meet, which is why tubal blockage is a common cause of female infertility. The ovaries make the ova and hormones, the cervix makes mucus, and the uterus is the site of implantation. Memory aid: ovary makes, tube transports, uterus implants.

A is wrong: Normal implantation occurs in the uterus, and implantation in the tube is an ectopic pregnancy.

B is wrong: Hormone production is the role of the ovaries, not the tubes.

D is wrong: Cervical mucus comes from the cervix, not the fallopian tubes.

202. During a reproductive health class in a Caloocan high school, the nurse describes the function of the vagina. Which statement is correct?

A. It contains glands that provide lubrication during arousal

B. It is the organ where the fertilized ovum implants and grows

C. It is the birth canal and the passage for menstrual blood

D. It secretes the mucus that keeps sperm alive near ovulation

Answer: C. It is the birth canal and the passage for menstrual blood

The vagina is a muscular canal that serves as the birth canal during delivery and as the passageway through which menstrual blood leaves the body. Cervical mucus is produced by the cervix, implantation occurs in the uterus, and lubrication during arousal comes mainly from the Bartholin's glands. Knowing each structure's single key function helps answer matching questions quickly on the PNLE. Memory aid: vagina is the passage, both for the baby and for menses.

A is wrong: Lubrication during arousal is mainly from the Bartholin's glands.

B is wrong: Implantation takes place in the uterus, not in the vagina.

D is wrong: Mucus that supports sperm is produced by the cervix, not the vagina.

203. A nurse reviews female internal genitalia with a group of student nurses in a Quezon City review center. Which pairing of structure and function is correct?

A. Cervix, produces cervical mucus

B. Fallopian tube, serves as the birth canal

C. Uterus, produces estrogen and progesterone

D. Ovary, transports the ovum to the uterus

Answer: A. Cervix, produces cervical mucus

According to the handout, the cervix produces cervical mucus, which becomes clear, thin and stretchy near ovulation under the influence of estrogen. The ovaries produce ova and hormones, the fallopian tubes transport the ovum, the uterus is the site of implantation, and the vagina is the birth canal. Changes in cervical mucus are the basis of the cervical mucus or Billings method of natural family planning. Exam tip: link the cervix with mucus and with Goodell's sign of softening.

B is wrong: The birth canal is the vagina, not the fallopian tube.

C is wrong: The uterus is where the fertilized egg implants, while hormones come from the ovaries.

D is wrong: The ovary produces the ovum and hormones, while the fallopian tube transports it.

204. A 60-year-old man scheduled for prostate surgery at a Pasig hospital asks the nurse what his prostate gland normally does. The best answer is that the prostate, together with the seminal vesicles,

A. carries the sperm from the epididymis upward

B. stores the sperm until they become fully mature

C. produces the sperm and the hormone testosterone

D. makes the seminal fluid that carries sperm

Answer: D. makes the seminal fluid that carries sperm

The prostate gland and the seminal vesicles produce seminal fluid, which nourishes the sperm and gives semen its volume. Sperm and testosterone are produced in the testes, sperm mature and are stored in the epididymis, and the vas deferens carries sperm from the epididymis to the urethra. The urethra then carries semen out during ejaculation. Sequence to memorize for the male tract: testes, epididymis, vas deferens, glands add fluid, urethra.

A is wrong: Transport from the epididymis is the role of the vas deferens.

B is wrong: Maturation and storage of sperm take place in the epididymis.

C is wrong: Sperm and testosterone are produced by the testes, not the prostate.

205. In the male reproductive system, which structure carries semen out of the body during ejaculation?

A. Seminal vesicle

B. Vas deferens

C. Epididymis

D. Urethra

Answer: D. Urethra

The urethra is the final passageway that carries semen out of the body during ejaculation, and it also carries urine. The vas deferens transports sperm from the epididymis to the urethra, the epididymis is where sperm mature and are stored, and the seminal vesicles add seminal fluid. In males the urethra therefore serves both the urinary and reproductive systems. Exam tip: the duct cut in vasectomy is the vas deferens, while the exit for semen is the urethra.

A is wrong: Seminal vesicles secrete fluid into the tract and are not the exit passage.

B is wrong: The vas deferens carries sperm only up to the urethra and does not open outside the body.

C is wrong: The epididymis stores and matures sperm but does not expel semen from the body.

206. Which external genital structure is correctly matched with its function?

A. Scrotum, contains erectile tissue for erection

B. Clitoris, secretes lubricating fluid in arousal

C. Penis, keeps the testes cooler for sperm making

D. Labia, protect vaginal and urethral openings

Answer: D. Labia, protect vaginal and urethral openings

The labia are folds of skin that protect the vaginal and urethral openings. The clitoris is a highly sensitive erectile structure, lubrication comes from the Bartholin's glands, the penis contains erectile tissue that allows erection, and the scrotum regulates the temperature of the testes for sperm production. Matching questions often swap the penis and scrotum functions, so read carefully. Memory aid: labia guard, clitoris feels, Bartholin lubricates, scrotum cools.

A is wrong: Erectile tissue is found in the penis, while the scrotum regulates testicular temperature.

B is wrong: The clitoris is a sensitive erectile organ, while lubrication comes from the Bartholin's glands.

C is wrong: Temperature regulation of the testes is the role of the scrotum, not the penis.

207. During a sexuality seminar for barangay youth, a participant asks the nurse what the term sex means as distinct from gender. The nurse explains that sex refers to

A. the biological body, such as anatomy and chromosomes

B. the inner sense of who a person feels himself to be

C. the persons to whom someone is sexually attracted

D. the broad term covering identity, body and attraction

Answer: A. the biological body, such as anatomy and chromosomes

In the handout, sex refers to your body, meaning the biological aspect such as anatomy, chromosomes and hormones. Gender is who you feel yourself to be, sexual orientation is whom you are sexually attracted to, and sexuality is the encompassing term that includes all of these. Keeping the four terms distinct helps answer questions about clients who describe their identity or attraction. Memory aid: sex is the body, gender is the mind, orientation is the heart, sexuality is the whole.

B is wrong: The inner sense of self as male or female describes gender.

C is wrong: Attraction toward others describes sexual orientation.

D is wrong: The encompassing term for all these aspects is sexuality.

208. A nursing student uses the MENS mnemonic to review the menstrual cycle. Which sequence of phases is correct?

A. Menstrual, estrogenic, ovulation, secretory

B. Menstrual, secretory, ovulation, estrogenic

C. Ovulation, menstrual, estrogenic, secretory

D. Estrogenic, menstrual, secretory, ovulation

Answer: A. Menstrual, estrogenic, ovulation, secretory

The MENS mnemonic lists the phases in order: Menstrual, Estrogenic or early follicular (proliferative), ovulation (the N), and Secretory or luteal (progestational). Menses sheds the endometrium, estrogen then rebuilds it, the LH surge causes ovulation, and the corpus luteum secretes progesterone in the secretory phase. If fertilization does not occur, hormones drop and the cycle restarts with menses. Tip: the proliferative phase is driven by estrogen and the secretory phase by progesterone.

B is wrong: The secretory phase follows ovulation, not menses, because it depends on the corpus luteum.

C is wrong: Ovulation occurs at mid cycle after the estrogenic phase, not at the start.

D is wrong: The cycle is counted from day 1 of menses, and the secretory phase follows ovulation.

209. A 22-year-old woman asks the nurse what exactly releases the egg during ovulation. The nurse explains that the LH surge causes

A. the corpus luteum to rupture and release the ovum

B. the mature Graafian follicle to release the ovum

C. the endometrium to shed together with the ovum

D. the primordial follicle to release the ovum directly

Answer: B. the mature Graafian follicle to release the ovum

Ovulation is triggered by the LH surge, which causes the mature or Graafian follicle to rupture and release an ovum into the fallopian tube. The remaining follicle then becomes the corpus luteum, which secretes progesterone during the secretory phase. Ovulation occurs about 14 days before the next menstrual period, and signs include a rise in basal temperature, mittelschmerz and stretchy cervical mucus. Memory aid: FSH grows the follicle, LH pops it.

A is wrong: The corpus luteum forms after ovulation from the ruptured follicle and does not release the ovum.

C is wrong: Shedding of the endometrium is menstruation, which happens when hormone levels fall.

D is wrong: Primordial follicles are immature and must first develop into a Graafian follicle.

210. During prenatal class, the nurse explains that the fetal heart, blood vessels, muscles and bones develop from which germ layer?

A. Mesoderm

B. Ectoderm

C. Endoderm

D. Trophoblast

Answer: A. Mesoderm

Organogenesis involves three germ layers: ectoderm, mesoderm and endoderm. The mesoderm forms the heart, blood vessels, blood, muscles, bones, kidneys and reproductive organs. The ectoderm forms the nervous system, skin, hair and nails, while the endoderm forms the lining of the gastrointestinal and respiratory tracts and glands such as the liver and pancreas. Memory aid: mesoderm is the middle layer that makes the moving and supporting parts.

B is wrong: The ectoderm forms the nervous system and skin, not the heart and bones.

C is wrong: The endoderm forms the linings of the digestive and respiratory tracts.

D is wrong: The trophoblast is the outer blastocyst layer that becomes the placenta, not a germ layer.

211. A nurse explains embryonic development to a woman at 7 weeks. Which structures arise from the endoderm?

A. Skeletal muscles, bones and the heart

B. Skin, hair, nails and tooth enamel

C. Linings of the digestive and respiratory tracts

D. Brain, spinal cord and peripheral nerves

Answer: C. Linings of the digestive and respiratory tracts

The endoderm is the innermost germ layer and forms the epithelial lining of the gastrointestinal and respiratory tracts, along with the liver, pancreas, thyroid and bladder lining. The ectoderm forms the nervous system and skin structures, while the mesoderm forms muscles, bones, the heart and blood vessels. All three layers appear during organogenesis, which the handout says is complete by about 8 weeks. Memory aid: endo means inside, so it lines the inside tubes.

A is wrong: Muscles, bones and the heart come from the mesoderm.

B is wrong: Skin and its appendages come from the ectoderm.

D is wrong: The nervous system comes from the ectoderm.

212. A woman at 5 weeks age of gestation at a Tondo health center asks what the developing baby is called at this point. Based on the handout, the nurse answers

A. embryo, since this stage lasts from 2 to 8 weeks

B. zygote, since this stage lasts until 12 weeks

C. blastocyst, since this stage lasts until 10 weeks

D. fetus, since this stage begins at 4 weeks

Answer: A. embryo, since this stage lasts from 2 to 8 weeks

The handout divides prenatal development into three stages: zygote for less than 2 weeks, embryo from 2 to 8 weeks, and fetus from 8 weeks until birth. At 5 weeks the developing baby is an embryo, which is the period when organs are forming and the risk from teratogens is greatest. Implantation occurs about 8 to 10 days after fertilization. Memory aid: 2 and 8 are the dividing lines, zygote before 2, embryo up to 8, fetus after 8.

B is wrong: The zygote stage lasts less than 2 weeks, not until 12 weeks.

C is wrong: The blastocyst is an early zygote stage before implantation, not a stage lasting to 10 weeks.

D is wrong: The fetal stage begins at 8 weeks, not 4 weeks.

213. A woman discovers she is pregnant at 6 weeks and worries about the medicines she took last month. Based on the handout timeline, by the end of which week are the head, heart, lungs and spinal cord formed?

A. 12th week

B. 8th week

C. 16th week

D. 4th week

Answer: D. 4th week

The handout timeline states that by the 4th week the head, heart, lungs and spinal cord are formed, and by the 8th week organogenesis is complete. This early period is when the embryo is most vulnerable to teratogens, often before the woman knows she is pregnant. That is why women of reproductive age are advised to take folic acid and avoid harmful drugs before conception. Timeline tip: 4 weeks basic structures, 8 weeks organogenesis complete, 12 weeks Doppler FHR.

A is wrong: At 12 weeks the milestones are FHR by Doppler and kidney function, not formation of the heart.

B is wrong: By the 8th week organogenesis is complete, but the basic structures appear earlier at 4 weeks.

C is wrong: At 16 weeks the milestones are FHR by fetoscope and quickening in multigravidas.

214. At a 12-week prenatal visit, the nurse hears the fetal heart with a Doppler. According to the handout, which other fetal milestone occurs at about this time?

A. The fetus reaches the age of viability

B. The primigravida first feels fetal movement

C. The kidneys begin to function and make urine

D. The lungs make enough surfactant for breathing

Answer: C. The kidneys begin to function and make urine

The handout lists two milestones at 12 weeks: the fetal heart rate can be detected by Doppler and the kidneys begin to function, producing urine. Fetal urine later becomes the main component of amniotic fluid, which is why kidney problems cause oligohydramnios. Lung maturity with an L/S ratio of 2:1 is at about 36 weeks, quickening in a primigravida is at 20 weeks, and viability is at 24 weeks. Tip: pair 12 weeks with Doppler and urine.

A is wrong: The age of viability is 24 weeks, not 12 weeks.

B is wrong: A primigravida usually feels quickening at about 20 weeks.

D is wrong: Adequate surfactant and mature lungs come near 36 weeks, shown by an L/S ratio of 2:1.

215. A G3P2 at 16 weeks age of gestation at a Malabon health center reports fluttering movements in her lower abdomen. The nurse interprets this finding as

A. too early, since quickening is never felt before 20 weeks

B. expected quickening, which multigravidas feel at 16 weeks

C. a sign of excess amniotic fluid that needs ultrasound

D. intestinal gas, since fetal movement begins at 24 weeks

Answer: B. expected quickening, which multigravidas feel at 16 weeks

According to the handout, quickening is felt at about 16 weeks in a multigravida and about 20 weeks in a primigravida. Women who have been pregnant before recognize the fluttering sensation earlier because they know what to expect. Quickening is a presumptive sign of pregnancy because it is subjective and reported by the mother. Memory aid: multi feels it first at 16, primi at 20.

A is wrong: Only a primigravida typically waits until about 20 weeks, while multigravidas feel it earlier.

C is wrong: Fluttering at 16 weeks is a normal finding and does not indicate polyhydramnios.

D is wrong: Fetal movement is felt well before 24 weeks, which is the age of viability.

216. According to the handout timeline, at about what age of gestation can the nurse first hear the fetal heart rate using a fetoscope?

A. 10 weeks

B. 28 weeks

C. 16 weeks

D. 24 weeks

Answer: C. 16 weeks

The handout gives a progression for hearing the fetal heart: by Doppler at 12 weeks, by fetoscope at 16 weeks and by an ordinary stethoscope at 20 weeks. Many textbooks place fetoscope detection at about 18 to 20 weeks, but for this review key to the handout value of 16 weeks. Fetal heart tones are a positive sign of pregnancy because they come only from the fetus. Memory aid: 12 Doppler, 16 fetoscope, 20 stethoscope, each step four weeks apart.

A is wrong: At 10 weeks only a Doppler device may detect the heartbeat, not a fetoscope.

B is wrong: At 28 weeks a fetoscope has long been usable, so this is not the earliest time.

D is wrong: By 24 weeks the heart can already be heard, since the fetoscope works from 16 weeks.

217. A mother asks how her baby receives protection against infections before birth. Which antibody crosses the placenta, with transfer noted from about 24 weeks in the handout?

A. IgA

B. IgG

C. IgM

D. IgE

Answer: B. IgG

IgG is the only immunoglobulin that crosses the placenta, giving the newborn passive natural immunity for the first months of life. The handout notes antibody transfer at about 24 weeks, and the transfer increases greatly in the third trimester, so preterm infants receive less. IgA is the main antibody in colostrum, while IgM is too large to cross the placenta. Memory aid: IgG, G for gestation, goes through the placenta.

A is wrong: IgA is mainly transferred through colostrum and breast milk, not the placenta.

C is wrong: IgM is a large molecule that does not cross the placenta.

D is wrong: IgE is involved in allergic reactions and is not the antibody transferred across the placenta.

218. A woman at 19 weeks at a Navotas health center tells the nurse she felt the baby move for the first time. How should the nurse classify this finding?

A. A danger sign, since movement should begin after 24 weeks

B. Presumptive sign, since the mother reports it

C. Positive sign, as it proves that a fetus is present

D. Probable sign, as it is objective and found by the examiner

Answer: B. Presumptive sign, since the mother reports it

Quickening, the first fetal movement felt by the mother, is a presumptive sign of pregnancy because it is subjective and reported by the woman. It appears in the PREGNANT mnemonic as noticeable fetal movement and can be mistaken for intestinal gas. By contrast, fetal movements palpated by an examiner are a positive sign. Exam tip: who detects it decides the category, mother means presumptive, examiner means probable or positive.

A is wrong: Movement felt at 19 weeks is normal and not a danger sign.

C is wrong: A positive sign requires detection by the examiner, such as palpable movement or ultrasound.

D is wrong: Probable signs are observed by the examiner, while quickening is felt and reported by the mother.

219. A woman at a barangay health station has a positive urine pregnancy test. How should the nurse classify this finding?

A. Diagnostic sign, since it confirms a live fetus

B. Positive sign, since the test detects only a fetus

C. Probable sign, since hCG may come from other causes

D. Presumptive sign, since it is reported by the woman

Answer: C. Probable sign, since hCG may come from other causes

A positive pregnancy test is a probable sign, included in the PREG TEST mnemonic, because it is objective but not conclusive. Tests detect hCG, which can also come from a hydatidiform mole, choriocarcinoma or some medications. Only fetal heart tones, fetal movements palpated by an examiner and ultrasound visualization of the fetus are positive signs. Memory aid: a test can lie, the fetus cannot, so the test is only probable.

A is wrong: A positive test does not confirm a live fetus, which requires positive signs such as FHT or ultrasound.

B is wrong: A pregnancy test detects hCG, which can be present without a viable fetus.

D is wrong: A test result is objective, while presumptive signs are subjective reports.

220. While auscultating a woman at 20 weeks, the nurse hears a soft blowing sound over the uterus that matches the maternal pulse. The nurse documents this as

A. funic souffle, a presumptive sign of pregnancy

B. uterine souffle, a probable sign of pregnancy

C. fetal heart tone, a positive sign of pregnancy

D. a maternal heart murmur that needs referral

Answer: B. uterine souffle, a probable sign of pregnancy

Uterine souffle is a soft blowing sound caused by blood flowing through the enlarged uterine vessels, and it is synchronized with the maternal pulse. It is a probable sign, the S in the PREG TEST mnemonic, because it reflects maternal circulation and not the fetus itself. Funic souffle, by contrast, matches the fetal heart rate and comes from blood in the umbilical cord. Tip: compare the sound with the mother's radial pulse to tell them apart.

A is wrong: Funic souffle matches the fetal heart rate and comes from the umbilical cord.

C is wrong: Fetal heart tones match the fetal rate of about 110 to 160 bpm, not the maternal pulse.

D is wrong: A blowing sound over the gravid uterus that matches the maternal pulse is an expected finding.

221. During a breast assessment at a prenatal visit in a Cebu clinic, the nurse notes dimpling of the skin over one breast. What is the best action?

A. Refer for further evaluation, since dimpling may suggest cancer

B. Teach nipple rolling exercises to prepare for breastfeeding

C. Reassure her that dimpling is a normal pregnancy breast change

D. Document it as a presumptive sign of pregnancy in the chart

Answer: A. Refer for further evaluation, since dimpling may suggest cancer

Breast enlargement and tenderness are presumptive signs of pregnancy, but the handout warns that dimpling of the breast may be associated with cancer. Skin dimpling or a peau d'orange appearance can signal an underlying malignancy even without a palpable lump. The nurse should document the finding and refer the client for further evaluation rather than attribute it to pregnancy. Exam tip: normal pregnancy changes are enlargement, tenderness and darker areolae, never dimpling.

B is wrong: Nipple preparation does not address a finding that may indicate cancer.

C is wrong: Dimpling is not a normal pregnancy change and should not be dismissed.

D is wrong: Presumptive breast signs are enlargement and tenderness, not dimpling.

222. A woman at 16 weeks at a Valenzuela health center worries about the dark line on her abdomen and the dark patches on her face. Which response by the nurse is best?

A. These are signs of a vitamin deficiency that needs injections

B. These are allergic reactions to the iron tablets you take

C. These are signs of liver disease that need tests right away
